24                The overnight hours of June 28, 

25   2005, my watch team and I received a message from 


                                                                3246

 1   the Pentagon and the White House Situation Room 

 2   in which we learned that a helicopter went down 

 3   in Afghanistan, killing 16 Americans.  We weren't 

 4   sure what was happening at that time.  We would 

 5   later find out that it was Operation Red Wings 

 6   that was sent to rescue a four-person Navy SEAL 

 7   team.

 8                What would eventually happen was the 

 9   deadliest day for Navy Special Warfare, which you 

10   all refer to as SEALS, since World War II.  It 

11   was a greatest single loss of life that community 

12   had ever experienced.  This year, this June 28th, 

13   we will celebrate the 10-year anniversary of that 

14   operation.  We're celebrating not only the lives 

15   of those who were lost, we're celebrating the 

16   heroism of Lieutenant Michael Murphy, a young man 

17   from the South Shore of Long Island, and we're 

18   celebrating the life of Marcus Luttrell, the lone 

19   survivor.

20                I also recall a day in October two 

21   years later when then-President Bush presented 

22   the Congressional Medal of Honor posthumously to 

23   Mr. Dan Murphy and Mrs. Maureen Murphy, Michael's 

24   mom and dad.  And my memory of that day is a 

25   president of the United States humbled by the 


                                                                3247

 1   actions of a young New Yorker, humbled by a young 

 2   lieutenant from the South Shore of Long Island.

 3                I also recall the president choking 

 4   back tears the entire day as he paid honor not 

 5   only to Michael Murphy, but to the members of the 

 6   teams who were lost that day and to all the 

 7   members who still serve.

 8                Mr. President, so many times 

 9   veterans are remembered with granite memorials 

10   and stone and marble, things that are cold.  And 

11   they're very important.  But today we get to 

12   honor a living tribute to Lieutenant Michael 

13   Murphy and to all of his shipmates, and that is 

14   the Michael Murphy Division of the U.S. Navy Sea 

15   Cadet Program.  And I'd ask them all to rise 

16   right now.

17                (Standing ovation.)

18                SENATOR CROCI:   There are two 

19   living memorials to that day and to those events.  

20   One is the USS Michael Murphy, named after the 

21   lieutenant.  And the other are the young men and 

22   women you see here today, their instructors, 

23   their commanding officer, and the volunteers, 

24   both their family members and people who just 

25   wanted to come out and volunteer.
